title: Piezoelectric micromanipulator dataset for hysteresis identification
version: Published Data in Brief article, PII S235234092030069X; supplement mmc1.zip
search: physical precision positioning piezoelectric actuator nonlinear hysteresis measured input voltage displacement dataset files Zenodo piezo closed loop control
Journal data article → Europe PMC full XML and original Elsevier supplementary archive → acquisition/plotting code and both raw CSVs; cross-check second repository copy.
rights: CC BY 4.0 per published article including its linked supplement (no separate terms in supplied archive). Attribute authors. Only new summaries and reader code included here.

mirror.test: Its mmc1.zip exactly matches the publisher ZIP.

measurements: Physically measured optical cantilever deflection (µm) against the published driving input (V). Driver waveform is generated by dSPACE, amplified externally. The supplied columns do not include independent terminal voltage or any clipping status. Frequency and amplitude change together between runs. Closed-loop tracking is not measured.
cleaning: Read columns 2–4 as time (s), optical output (µm), driving voltage (V) following the authors’ MATLAB. Leave DC offset in the first trace and evaluate at the midpoint of its recorded voltage span; direction differences and cubic curves with intercept are offset-invariant. Retain all first-trace rows and only t>5 s of 150 V as in author code. The second trace first has nonzero input at 3.2572 s; its full time column, 50,001 rows/10 s, and Table 1 agree on about 0.2 ms between samples. Article prose says 20 ms. Do not apply that value to the data.
analysis: Start and finish cycles at consecutive linearly interpolated rising midpoint crossings; require one falling crossing in the interior. Integrate y du on measured piecewise-linear segments. Compare a cubic of normalized driving input with separate cubics for rising and falling directions on the last chronological cycles of the same recording. Falling/rising label carries forward across equal input values. Lag, rate response and hysteresis can all contribute; two records cannot identify their independent causes. Cycles in one run are not independent experiments.
reproduce: Python 3 + NumPy: python derive_piezo.py ORIGINAL_mmc1.zip OUTPUT_DIR
